Day 1 · Sun 27 Sep

Colombo

Landing · 20 min to the beach

We land at Colombo and go straight to Negombo, the beach town next to the airport. Long sand, fishing boats drawn up on it, good seafood.

Afternoon
Land at Colombo, 16:15Our driver meets us in the arrivals hall with a name board.
Evening
At the hotel, unpacked
Night
Dinner by the sea
Negombo · beachfront hotel
Day 2 · Mon 28 Sep

Kandy

3½ hours inland, up into the hills
🎂 Birthday

The old royal capital, wrapped around a lake in green hills — and where the birthday lands. The Temple of the Tooth is the holiest Buddhist site in the country, and the evening ceremony — an hour of drummers, horns and people carrying lotus flowers — is the thing to be there for. Quite a way to spend a birthday evening.

Morning
Drive up, stopping at a spice gardenCinnamon, cardamom and pepper growing on the bush
Afternoon
Peradeniya Botanical GardensFlat shaded paths, huge old trees. No steps.
Evening
Temple of the Tooth for the evening ceremony, then birthday dinner
Kandy · hilltop, above the city lights. Pack before bed.
Day 3 · Tue 29 Sep

Nuwara Eliya

3 hours up · the hill station the British built

The strangest town in Sri Lanka, and the prettiest. The British built it as a hill station and it never quite stopped being one — a red-brick Tudor post office, colonial bungalows with rose gardens, a racecourse, log fires at night. They call it Little England. Six thousand feet up, cool all year, tea in every direction. The afternoon and evening are completely free.

Late morning
A gentle start, up through the teaStopping at Ramboda Falls, and anywhere else worth stopping
Midday
At the hotel in time for lunch
Afternoon
FreeThe town, the lake, a tea factory, the spa — or the fire and a book
Evening
Tea at the Grand Hotel, then a long dinner
Heritance Tea Factory · an old tea factory turned hotel, alone in the tea fields. Bring something warm.
Day 4 · Wed 30 Sep

The mountain train

3½ hours to Ella, sitting down

The old hill railway runs along the mountainside through tea gardens, tunnels and stone viaducts — often called one of the most beautiful train rides in the world. Reserved seats, windows open. The driver takes the bags by road.

Morning
A working tea estateLeaf picked, dried, rolled, graded — then tasted
Late morning
Board the train at Nanu Oya
Afternoon
Arrive Ella, check in, do nothing
Evening
Sunset through the gap in the mountains
Two nights · Ella — chalets built into a tea slope
Day 5 · Thu 1 Oct · Rest day

A day off

No packing, no driving, no schedule

The one day we stay put. The Nine Arch Bridge — a stone railway viaduct standing in the jungle — is a flat ten-minute walk from where the tuk-tuk stops.

Early
An optional climb up the hill for sunrise, and a zipline afterFor whoever fancies it. Everyone else, breakfast at leisure.
Whenever
Breakfast on the terrace
Late morning
Nine Arch Bridge, then a long lunch in the village
Rest of it
A waterfall, the pool, or the view — all optional
Ella again · same room, nothing to pack
Day 6 · Fri 2 Oct

Mirissa

4½ hours down to the sea

The longest drive, and the land changes completely on the way down — mountains and tea give way to flat green country, then coconut palms. Mirissa is a curved beach with a famous sunset.

Morning
Leave Ella, lunch on the way
Afternoon
Reach Mirissa, check inNothing planned. The pool, or a walk to the sand.
Evening
Sunset, then dinner by the water
Two nights · Mirissa — beach hotel with a pool
Day 7 · Sat 3 Oct

Galle

45 minutes along the coast, back for dinner

A four-hundred-year-old Dutch fort built out into the sea — cobbled lanes, a white lighthouse, old houses full of little shops, and wide stone walls you can walk right around. Lovely even in the rain.

Morning
Free — pool, beach, or the palm hill up the road
Afternoon
Into the fort — the lanes, the lighthouse, a café
Sunset
On the ramparts, with the whole town out walking
Mirissa · pack tonight, and ask for breakfast boxes
